items.title: Bringing back open-market buybacks through stock exchanges is the right decision
items.description: SEBI’s decision to restore open-market buybacks through stock exchanges marks a pragmatic regulatory shift that supports efficient capital allocation. The move recognises evolving market dynamics while maintaining safeguards, giving companies greater flexibility to return surplus capital and strengthening confidence in market-led decision-making.

items.title: Father’s Day: The financial legacy children truly inherit
items.description: Indian fathers are redefining legacy, moving beyond just assets to financial behaviour. The rise of micro-investing and digital platforms allows for consistent, small-scale participation, making wealth creation an everyday habit. This shift, driven by accessibility and automation, teaches children valuable lessons in discipline and long-term planning, shaping a more enduring inheritance than mere wealth.

items.title: Earnings of OMCs seen weak as Q1FY27 under-recoveries bite: Report
items.description: Oil companies are projected to experience ongoing challenges through FY27, primarily due to anticipated under-recoveries in Q1FY27, with LPG losses being a considerable issue. Although recent declines in crude prices provide short-term relief, ongoing market volatility and required inventory adjustments are expected to squeeze profit margins. A notable threat includes the government's possible retraction of excise duty cuts to mitigate revenue shortfalls.

items.title: A stock trader’s guide to navigating rare ‘Super El Niño’
items.description: As fears over the Iran conflict ease, investors are turning their attention to climate risk, with a potential “Super El Niño” emerging as a key market variable. From agriculture and energy to insurance and financials, the weather event could reshape sector outlooks, affect inflation trends and influence investment decisions globally.

items.title: Dividends & bonus issues: LIC, Asian Paints among 35 stocks turning ex-record date this week. How many do you own?
items.description: Around 35 companies, including LIC, HUL, Asian Paints and IndusInd Bank, have fixed record dates for dividends, bonus issues and buybacks in the upcoming week. Investors must hold shares before the record date to qualify for corporate actions, though additional announcements may follow.

items.title: Will Sensex, Nifty bounce back on Monday? Iran peace deal risks among 5 factors to drive D-St this week
items.description: Indian stock markets experienced a sharp decline on Friday, breaking a five-day winning streak. Key factors influencing Dalal Street next week include potential US-Iran peace deal risks, volatile oil prices, a significant sell-off in IT stocks, the rupee's performance against the dollar, and a return of foreign institutional investors as net buyers. These elements will shape market sentiment in the coming days.

items.title: Will Nifty hit 25,000 this month? Key levels to watch in the week ahead
items.description: Nifty eyes a potential up move, with immediate targets at 24,300–24,600, though a dash to 25,000 this month appears uncertain. The IT index remains technically weak, while the defence index shows strong momentum, hitting a 52-week high. Experts recommend buying Radico Khaitan and Redington, citing bullish continuation setups and recovery signs respectively.
